AI work journal

This project uses an Obsidian-based work journal to preserve useful context from AI-assisted work.

Log location

All AI work logs for this project are stored inside the project repository in:

AI_logs/

Create the directory if it does not already exist.

Use one Markdown file for each substantive working session. Name files using:

YYYY-MM-DD-short-description.md

For example:

AI_logs/2026-09-21-local-calibration.md
AI_logs/2026-09-22-validation-analysis.md

If more than one unrelated substantive session occurs on the same day, add a short distinguishing description. Avoid creating multiple files for small tasks that are part of the same continuous session.

The AI log is part of the project’s working documentation and should remain understandable independently of the original AI conversation.

General principle

Keep a concise record of substantive work performed with the AI assistant. The journal is intended to capture information that will be useful later, especially:

  • what was being worked on;
  • what was changed or implemented;
  • important technical or scientific decisions;
  • important results or conclusions;
  • files that were substantially modified;
  • unresolved questions and next steps.

Do not attempt to record every command, debugging step, or conversational exchange.

What counts as substantive work

Create or update the work log when one or more of the following occurs:

  • code, analysis, documentation, or manuscript text is substantially changed;
  • an implementation or analysis approach is selected or changed;
  • an important bug is identified or resolved;
  • a meaningful result is produced or interpreted;
  • a decision is made that is likely to matter in a future session;
  • several related files are modified as part of a task;
  • a substantial investigation, literature search, or technical discussion is completed.

Routine actions such as formatting, small typo fixes, package installation, file inspection, or unsuccessful exploratory commands generally do not need to be logged unless they affect an important decision.

Log content

Each log file should begin with YAML metadata:

---
type: ai-work-log
date: YYYY-MM-DD
project: PROJECT_NAME
source: codex (or claude, with version)
summary: "One sentence describing the work accomplished."
---

Set source to the assistant used for the session, for example:

  • codex
  • posit-assistant
  • chatgpt

The summary must be a concise sentence that can also be displayed in the project’s Obsidian Daily Note.

Use the following structure for the body:

# Short descriptive title

## Objective

Briefly describe what we were trying to accomplish.

## Work completed

- Summarize substantive work performed.
- Focus on outcomes rather than individual commands.
- Mention important implementation details where useful.

## Decisions

- Record decisions that should persist into future work.
- Include important methodological or design choices.

Omit this section if no meaningful decisions were made.

## Files changed

- `path/to/file`
- `path/to/another/file`

Include only files that were substantively changed.

## Results

Record important numerical results, validation outcomes, findings, or conclusions.

Omit this section when there are no meaningful results to record.

## Open items

- Record unresolved questions.
- Record important follow-up tasks.
- Record known limitations that should be revisited.

Omit this section if there are no open items.

Logging behaviour

When a substantive task reaches a natural stopping point:

  1. Review the work completed during the current session.
  2. Determine whether an existing log in AI/ represents the current working session.
  3. If so, update that log.
  4. Otherwise, create a new log using the naming convention above.
  5. Update the YAML summary so it accurately describes the work completed so far.
  6. Keep the log concise and focused on information useful in a future work session.

Do not create a separate journal entry for every small request within the same continuous work session. Prefer one evolving entry describing the meaningful work completed during that session.

The user can explicitly request logging using phrases such as:

  • log this
  • update the work log
  • write the session log

When explicitly requested, update the log even if the work would normally fall below the threshold for automatic logging.

Writing style

Logs should be:

  • concise;
  • factual;
  • useful several months later;
  • understandable without rereading the complete AI conversation;
  • specific about decisions and results;
  • written in Markdown.

Prefer:

Changed local calibration to estimate a segment-specific pixel effect while retaining the age-dependent shape of the assigned RSYC.

rather than:

We discussed different approaches and eventually decided to make some changes to calibration.

Information that must not be logged

Never place the following in the work journal:

  • passwords;
  • authentication tokens;
  • API keys;
  • private credentials;
  • environment secrets;
  • confidential information unrelated to the scientific or technical work being documented.

Do not copy large blocks of source code or entire AI conversations into the journal unless the user explicitly requests this.

Relationship to git

The work journal complements git history; it does not duplicate it.

Git records what changed in the repository.

The AI journal should emphasize why it changed, what was decided, what was learned, and what remains to be done.
